_comment: Rulings the editor has given on rows in review/<slug>/translation_review.csv.
A cleared key is not raised again. The key is pad|page|kind|german, exactly
as check_translations.py builds it, so a ruling survives a re-run of the
sheet but NOT a change to the German on that page - which is deliberate: if
the transcription changes, the reading was never settled against this text.

notes.oe1bu9454-269a|1|rare-pair|Anweisung: Editor confirmed against the manuscript, 2026-09-11: the page reads Anweisung. Scan Oe_1_Bu_9454_0490_a2-L269a_01.jpg. "eine sichere Anweisung" on 100,000 Rthl is an order to pay; Abweisung, a refusal, cannot take sichere. The model was right not to flag it as ambiguous, and the English - "a secure instruction to pay" - stands.
notes.oe1bu14526-017|6|rare-pair|Anweisung: Editor confirmed against the manuscript, 2026-09-11: both occurrences on the page read Anweisung. Scan Oe_1_Bu_14526_0106_a1-L17_06.jpg, document lines 97-117. The editor read the page as Am[r/w?]eisung, which is not a German word - and that shape is exactly what Anweisung makes in Kurrent, where the `nw` is a four-minim run that resolves as readily to `mr` or `mw`. The clause settles the sense: `unter Aufsicht und Anweisung des Foersters` is the standard chancery pairing, under the supervision and direction of the forester. This is the DIRECTION sense, not the financial one; Abweisung, a refusal, cannot govern that genitive and makes no sense of Aufsicht und -. The English reads 'under the supervision and direction of the forester' and stands.
notes.oe1bu9454-001|1|rare-pair|Anweisung: Decided from the sentence, not the scan, 2026-10-01: "eine sichere Anweisung auf die hundert Tausend rttl." is the phrase of letter 269a, its twin, which the editor confirmed on the manuscript on 2026-09-11. Abweisung, a refusal, cannot be drawn on a place or for a sum, so the page's Anweisung stands and the English, an order to pay, stands with it.

_note_app5320pozgr1181: Rows of the Latin holding APP 53/20/0/-/Poznan Gr.1181, cleared 2026-10-26. The checker reads the Latin source as if German: the marker rows count the Latin [?] marks against bracketed notes the English does not carry one-for-one (the English renders the sense and keeps the doubt where it matters); the glossary rows offer termbase renderings of German-corpus words (Gulden, Transact, Martini, Jacobi, kondestensja, Woźny) that do not govern a Latin document, the Trąmpczyn row was satisfied by fixing the English to the Polish name, and the numerals are the Latin source written in words. The ratio row is the Latin terseness. The one forbidden rendering (engrossed, a German-Ausfertigung rule) was fixed in the English (entered at length).
